note: sign(enabled: bool) returns "+"/"-" via if enabled {..} else {..} - textbook flag-argument, a Sign enum or two named constants would read better at call sites like sign(pcre2).
matched_stripped(path, is_dir: bool): is_dir is an operand of 'if !glob.is_only_dir() || is_dir' to decide whether a dir-only glob still counts as a match.
matched_with_errors_impl: is_dir is branched on repeatedly (if !is_dir && !satisfies_min, if !is_dir, if is_dir) to decide min/max-depth and descend behavior.
Override::matched: is_dir is an operand of 'if mat.is_none() && self.num_whitelists() > 0 && !is_dir' controlling whitelist-override semantics for non-dirs.
Types::matched: is_dir is an operand of 'if is_dir || self.set.is_empty()' since file-type globs never apply to directories.

WalkBuilder::skip_stdout(&mut self, yes: bool) - idiomatic Rust builder setter, correctly matches the rule's mechanical definition; a defensible style choice some may not consider a real smell. Candidate for a future &mut-self-builder exemption if this class of finding turns out noisy in practice.

RegexMatcherBuilder::crlf(&mut self, yes: bool): same idiomatic builder-setter shape as the already-marked skip_stdout - if yes {..} else {..} then stores yes into config.crlf; mechanically correct, arguably not worth flagging as a smell in this pattern.

minimal_heap_limit(&self, multi_line: bool): multi_line is the first branch of an if/else-if/else chain selecting how the required search buffer size is computed - a real computed-flag branch, not a builder setter.
